transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Collins (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Head of ML, Elysian), Tom Nguyen (Platform Eng), Priya Sharma (Security), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Dana from our infra team. how are you all?
[00:10] Marta: Hi, thanks. doing well. excited to talk through the poc scope.
[00:15] Dana: hey all, quick agenda, i want to understand your current traffic, success metrics, then propose a bench plan — qps, concurrency, token shapes, and timelines.
[00:25] Tom: sounds good. i'll kick off with context — we run a document-processing assistant across retail and mortgage teams. about 80% of requests are short chat style, 20% are long-form summarization.
[00:40] Marta: yeah, we use an internal LLM pipeline today on prem, but it's flaky during month-end. want to validate performance and cost before moving to any managed solution.
[00:50] Samir: great — high level success criteria? latency p95, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens usually. what are your targets?
[01:05] Tom: p95 under 350ms ideally for the chat flows. for summarization we can tolerate higher, like p95 800ms. overall target is to serve 25 QPS steady across peak, with bursts up to 70 QPS for short windows.
[01:20] Dana: ok that's helpful. when you say 25 QPS steady, is that globally or regionally?
[01:25] Tom: mostly US-east, a smaller EU peak. plan is single-region for the poc.
[01:30] Marta: concurrency wise, our frontend opens ~12 concurrent websocket streams during peak per service, with each stream sending 1-2 messages per minute, but spikes happen.
[01:45] Dana: so concurrency target of around 12-16 to model. that matches our initial sizing.
[01:50] Priya: security note — we need SOC2 type II and KMS integration, keys must be customer-managed if we go private. also data retention zero by default for hosted.
[02:05] Samir: noted, we will share SOC2 and KMS docs.

[02:20] Dana: can you walk through the token distribution? avg input/output lengths?
[02:30] Tom: average user prompt is ~45-80 tokens. responses vary: for chat approx 60-140 tokens; for summarization avg input 600 tokens and output 300-500 tokens. overall across traffic: mean input ~70, mean output ~120.
[02:50] Marta: percentiles: p50 input 40, p90 input 220, p99 input ~1200 (rare long docs). output p50 90, p90 320.
[03:05] Dana: perfect — that p99 long tail will affect GPU memory and kv cache. we'll plan tests including long-sequence runs.

[03:20] Samir: what are success criteria beyond latency? e.g., hallucination rate, tokenization differences, cost per inference?
[03:30] Marta: accuracy is measured via a labeled set of 1k prompts we can provide. we want <5% regression in our key QA metrics compared to baseline.
[03:40] Tom: and cost target is 40% improvement over our current on-prem unit cost, if possible.

[03:55] Dana: ok for modeling i'll propose two workload shapes: 1) chat steady-state: 25 QPS, avg in/out 70/120 tokens, concurrency 12; 2) summarization batch: 3 QPS but high tokens (600 in / 350 out) concurrency 6; 3) spike test: 70 QPS short burst for 2-5 minutes. we'll include a long-tail test for p99 sequences.
[04:20] Tom: that seems right. also caching behavior: we have lots of repeated prefixes for short chat followups; prefix/KV caching would help. do you model that?
[04:35] Dana: yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; in benchmarks we can toggle cache on/off to show delta. expect 20-35% token cost reduction in lots of prefix reuse workloads depending on cache hit rate.
[04:50] Marta: quantization — we might want to use int8 or 4-bit for cost. how does that affect latency/quality?
[04:58] Dana: we typically benchmark fp16, int8, and 4-bit quantized variants. int8 gives decent perf with minimal quality loss for most models; 4-bit can save more on memory and cost but we evaluate quality regressions with your labeled set. we'll include quality/latency/cost tradeoff charts.

[05:20] Samir: timeline — how long should the POC run? we usually do a 2-week technical POC: first week ingest sample traffic + baseline runs, second week sustained load and focused benchmarks, then results and recommendation. does that fit your procurement timeline?
[05:36] Marta: yes ideally start by end of month. decision window 6 weeks after POC.
[05:42] Tom: for the bench we can give you anonymized traffic logs by Friday.
[05:48] Priya: security review will take 2 weeks but we can run security QA in parallel.

[06:00] Dana: benchmark metrics we'll collect: p50/p90/p95 latency, tail p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, throughput (reqs/sec), GPU utilization, memory pressure, and failure/error rates. we'll also capture cold-start behavior for model warmup and KV cache warmups.
[06:20] Tom: for load generation, we prefer using real sample distribution with the same token histograms and inter-arrival times. can you accept a k6 or locust script?
[06:30] Dana: yes, dockerized k6 or python load runners are fine. we'll provide a docker image that hits Redwood hosted endpoints or your private POC endpoint.

[06:40] Samir: quick question — are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the POC?
[06:45] Marta: want to test hosted first for speed, but will need dedicated if latency/cost don't meet targets or for isolation.
[06:52] Dana: makes sense. we'll run hosted compare then run a dedicated config if needed. dedicated sizing will be proposed after we see steady-state throughput and memory for your model choices.

[07:05] Liam: on observability — we need token-level cost breakdown per route and trace correlation to our logs. can we integrate our tracing?
[07:15] Samir: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token/latency dashboards and we emit trace headers that you can correlate; we'll share docs.

[07:25] Marta: for the benchmark, what sample size do you need?
[07:30] Dana: for stable latency estimates we'll do sustained runs of 30-60 minutes per scenario and then a 24-hour soak for cost extrapolation; total synthetic requests per scenario about 100k-500k depending on tokens.
[07:45] Tom: ok. for p95 confidence we want enough samples. good.

[07:55] Priya: on compliance, we need an option for customer-managed KMS and audit log retention 1 year. is that possible?
[08:05] Samir: yes for Private deployments we support customer KMS; audit logs retention is pluggable and we can put details in the security doc.

[08:18] Dana: any model constraints — are you evaluating open models or closed ones?
[08:24] Marta: we want to try a 13B open model first (our current baseline) and then test a few variants (13B quantized, 30B distil). also evaluate possible Redwood-verified models.
[08:35] Dana: good — we'll profile memory and throughput for 13B FP16, 13B int8 and 4-bit buckets and report GPU reqs to hit your 25 QPS target. initial estimate: with continous batching a single A10G-like GPU could handle ~20-30 QPS for short chat with avg tokens ~200, but long summaries will need more memory/throughput. we'll confirm in bench.
[08:58] Tom: that estimate helps for procurement.

[09:05] Samir: risks/assumptions — we assume tokenization match, no large pre/post processing differences, and that your labeled set can be used to evaluate quality offline.
[09:18] Marta: agreed. we'll sanitize and share the labeled set.

[09:25] Dana: recap of next steps: 1) Samir sends POC proposal and pricing with hosted vs dedicated options 2) Dana shares benchmark plan + dockerized k6 scripts 3) Elysian exports traffic stats and labeled set 4) schedule benchmark run for week of 3/30 5) Redwood shares SOC2/KMS docs.
[09:50] Tom: sounds good. one more thing — cost modeling, can you give a rough cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated after bench?
[10:00] Samir: yes we'll provide cost model ranges and exact numbers post-bench. usually we show unit economics with and without prefix caching and with quantization.

[10:12] Marta: thanks all, this is action-oriented.
[10:16] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with docs and the proposal.
[10:20] Dana: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: audio had a few interruptions; some acronyms transcribed as K V cash or kv cache inconsistently. There are natural speech hesitations.

Bench plan summary (attached as reference link): https://redwood.ai/bench-plans/elysian-2026-03 (note: placeholder link).
